title: Usage event ingestion API
goal: The usage event ingestion API: authenticated devices post batches of metered usage events that are validated, deduplicated by event id, attributed to the right workspace and stored for aggregation.
scope_in: POST /v1/usage/events (scope usage:write, device principal, Idempotency-Key required): body {events:[{id,type,qty,at,session_id?,agent_id?}]} up to 500 events and 1 MiB.

Validation: type in agent_minutes|tokens_in|tokens_out|queue_items|relay_bytes, qty non-negative integer within per-type caps, `at` within the last 31 days and at most 60 s in the future, id format and uniqueness.
Dedup by (workspace, event id): ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; response reports accepted and duplicate counts.
Workspace attribution: session_id -> the session's workspace (caller must be a participant); else token `wsp` claim; else the user's personal workspace.
Per-device rate limit 60 requests/min (bucket from CT-PAGE) and per-workspace daily event cap.
Raw usage_event table (append-only) and a Redis stream hint for B075.
scope_out: Aggregation, quota percentages and warnings: B075/B076.
Relay-side counters (relay_bytes, queue_items recorded by the relay): B075 reads them; this lane only takes client reports.
Idempotency and rate-limit middleware implementations: B024/B023 (used here).
build_against: Fastify inject with test device tokens, in-memory idempotency store and rate limiter (B024/B023 test doubles), Postgres container for usage_event; fixtures of 500-event batches generated in the test.
interfaces: POST /v1/usage/events {events: UsageEvent[]} -> 200 {accepted:number, duplicates:number}  | 422 problem+json with errors[] pointers like /events/3/qty
UsageIngest.ingest(principal: DevicePrincipal, events: UsageEvent[]): Promise<{accepted:number, duplicates:number}>
Table usage_event(workspace_id, event_id, type, qty bigint, at, session_id null, agent_id null, device_id, received_at, pk(workspace_id, event_id)); index (workspace_id, type, at)
Per-type qty caps: agent_minutes <= 1440, tokens_in/out <= 2_000_000_000, queue_items <= 10_000, relay_bytes <= 2^40
acceptance: POST without Idempotency-Key returns `idempotency_key_required`; replay with the same key and body returns the stored response with Idempotency-Replayed: true and inserts nothing new.
A batch of 500 valid events returns 200 {accepted:500, duplicates:0} in < 500 ms on the Postgres container; 501 events returns 422; body > 1 MiB returns 413.
Re-sending 100 already-ingested event ids (new Idempotency-Key) returns {accepted:0, duplicates:100} and totals do not change.

An event with qty -1, fractional qty, unknown type, or `at` 2 minutes in the future makes the whole batch return 422 with errors[].pointer '/events/<i>/qty' (or /type, /at), `out_of_range` style code, and stores nothing from the batch.
A token with scope usage:write only for another user's session_id (caller not a participant) returns 403; an API key principal returns 403 (usage is device-reported).
Events for session_id are attributed to that session's workspace even when the token wsp claim differs; without session_id the token wsp claim is used, else the personal workspace.
The 61st request within a minute from one device returns 429 with Retry-After and RateLimit-* headers.
Two concurrent requests carrying the same event ids insert each id exactly once (unique key), both return 200.
tests: usage.validate.test.ts: field rules, caps, time window
usage.authz.test.ts: scope, principal types, participant check
usage.contract.test.ts: schema validation and error shape (CT-ERR)
guardrails: MUST reject the whole batch on any invalid event; partial acceptance would corrupt client retry logic.
MUST scope dedupe by workspace so a client cannot probe other workspaces' event ids.
MUST NOT store anything beyond the contract fields plus device id and receive time; no message or path data.
MUST NOT block ingestion when the workspace is over quota; usage is a fact and still recorded (quota is enforced elsewhere).
qty and `at` MUST be validated server-side; client clock is not trusted beyond the stated window.
failure_modes: DB unavailable -> 503 with retry_after_s; client retries with the same Idempotency-Key and event ids.
Redis stream hint fails -> ingestion still succeeds; B075's periodic sweep finds new rows by received_at.
Idempotency store down -> fail closed with 503 for this required-key endpoint.
